title: Sui Dynasty
capsule: The Sui dynasty (581–618 CE) reunified China after nearly four centuries of fragmentation following the collapse of the Han, with Emperor Wen (Yang Jian) conquering the southern Chen dynasty in 589 and imposing a single administrative system. Emperor Yang (r. 604–618) completed the Grand Canal linking the Yellow and Yangtze rivers, but his ruinous campaigns against Goguryeo and massive conscription triggered widespread rebellion. In 618 a Li Yuan — one of Yang's generals — captured Chang'an and founded the Tang dynasty, while the last Sui emperor was assassinated in Jiangdu.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well-documented through dynastic administrative records (Suishu) and archaeological surveys; the core commandery system provides firm boundaries, though frontier zones toward Central Asia and Vietnam are approximated from tributary relationships rather than direct administration.
